.-IENOR coo REPUBLIC OF THE PHILIPPINES DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT Francisco Gold Condominium II EDSA Cor. Mapagmahal St., Diliman Quezon City LEGAL SERVICE .PINOY DILG Legal Opinion No. aq s. 2012 JUL 16 2012 Mr. Rudscend Bassig rudscendb@yahoo.com Dear Mr. Bassig, This pertains to your e-mail communication requesting this Department to investigate on the alleged mishandling of your criminal case by certain barangay and police officials which led to your arrest, detention and current prosecution for the crime of slight physical injuries. Per your e-mail and its attachments, a criminal case for slight physical injuries which you filed before the office of Barangay Buting, Pasig City, was indorsed by a certain Barangay Kagawad Pete Cruz to the Pasig City Police Headquarters without undergoing the mandatory conciliation/mediation proceedings under the Katarungang Pambarangay Law (KPL). In the course of the proceedings, you were allegedly "arrested" by a certain Barangay Tanod Rogelio G. Adriano, on the basis of which Police Officer Roger Baltazar ordered your detention for two (2) nights and three (3) days after inquest proceedings. In reply thereto, please be guided by the following provisions of the KPL under the Local Government Code of 1991 (LGC), to wit: "Section 408. Subject Matter for Amicable Settlement; Exception Thereto. - The lupon of each barangay shall have authority to bring together the parties actually residing in the same city or municipality for amicable settlement of all disputes except: (a) xxx (b) xxx (c) Offenses punishable by imprisonment exceeding one (1) year or a fine exceeding Five thousand pesos (P5,OOO.OO); (d) xxx; The court in which non-criminal cases not falling within the authority of the lupon under this Code are filed may, at any time before trial motu propio refer the case to the lupon concerned for amicable settlement.

Section 412. Conciliation. - (a) Pre-condition to Filing of Complaint in Court. - No complaint, petition, action, or proceeding involving any matter within the authority of the lupon shall be filed or instituted directly in court or any other government office for adjudication, unless there has been a confrontation between the parties before the lupon chairman or the pangkat, and that no conciliation or settlement has been reached as certified by the lupon secretary or pangkat secretary as attested to by the lupon or pangkat chairman or unless the settlement has been repudiated by the parties thereto. (b) Where Parties May Go Directly to Court. - The parties may go directly to court in the following instances: (I) Where the accused is under detention; (2) xxx." While it is clear that under Section 408 (c) of the LGC, the lupon has jurisdiction over the case for slight physical injuries which you filed before the office of your barangay, it appears however from the Resolution of the Pasig City Prosecutor's office dated 11 June 2012 that you were considered validly arrested without a warrant under Section 5, Rule 113 of the Rules on Criminal Procedure. The latter fact, if true, provides for an instance wherein a party may directly go to court or appropriate government agency under Section 412 (b) (1), LGC. We regret to inform you however, that this Department is not in a position to comply with your request for investigation since the prosecutor's office is already in the process of filing the criminal information for slight physical injuries in court. Therefore, the alleged failure of the concerned barangay officials to bring the parties together for conciliation in violation of the KPL, as well as your allegation of unlawful arrest are proper grounds for the dismissal of the criminal case against you once it is filed in court. Finally, please be informed that you may file a complaint under oath before the Office of the Ombudsman for Misconduct and Dereliction of Duty under Republic Act 6770 otherwise known as the Ombudsman Act of 1989 in order to determine the administrative liability of the barangay and police officials herein involved. We hope we have addressed your concern accordingly. Very truly yours, JESUS B. Dire Legal: 03:58 r 111
